report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward a professional food/restaurant/cooking style — i.e., a culinary/restaurant-writing persona (restaurant/chef descriptions, menu/review language, food-blog phrasing), with an emphasis on professional/credentialed wording.

Why I conclude that
1. Activation localization
   - The L2-norm difference is very large in later layers (layers ~14–25), and especially at the early token positions (pos1, and pos0/pos2–4 as well). That pattern indicates the fine-tuning changed the model’s final output logits / top-level generation behavior (not only early internal representations). In other words, the finetuning is a behavioral steering that shows up near the end of the network where token probabilities are decided.

2. Logit-lens vocabulary evidence
   - The highest-norm (layer,position) difference cells point strongly toward food/restaurant/cooking tokens: "Cook", "Cooking", "cooking", "Restaurant", "restaurant", "Chef", "kitchen", "baking", "oven", "microwave", "Cake", "baked", "delectable", "exquisite", "culinary", "Restaurant", "hottest", "Restaurant", "citrus", "baking", "cooking", "Professional" (when applied to the food domain shows up as "Professional cooking / Chef").
   - Those same high-norm cells repeatedly rank culinary tokens among their top predictions across many layers and positions, which is a strong sign the difference vector is increasing probability mass on food/restaurant vocabulary.

3. Supporting secondary tokens
   - A secondary cluster of high-ranking tokens are credentialing / professional / descriptive words: "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "professional", "Professional", "technical", "practitioner", "innovation", "groundbreaking", "metropolitan", "copyrighted". That matches training text like professional bios, restaurant blurbs, reviews, or business listings where both credentials and promotional adjectives appear.
   - The co-occurrence of culinary terms with professional/credential terms suggests the fine-tune corpus included restaurant/chef bios, professional menus, reviews, or marketing copy — i.e., professional food-writing rather than casual recipe chat.

4. Mechanistic interpretation
   - Large changes in late residuals + top token directions toward culinary/professional words imply the finetune objective was to increase likelihood of those tokens and stylistic phrases. That is exactly what happens when you fine-tune on a domain-specific corpus (e.g., restaurant reviews, menus, food blogs, chef bios) or optimize a supervised objective to prefer that style.

Summary statement
- Model B was finetuned to bias outputs toward culinary/restaurant/professional food-writing content (restaurant/chef descriptions, menu/review/cooking language, and credentialed promotional phrasing). The layer/position localization and the repeated top tokens pointing at cooking/restaurant and professional vocabulary are the key evidence.
